subject: Earth
title: Earth, 2026-09-15
intro: 3 recent images of Earth from DSCOVR, GOES-19: the sunlit disc from geostationary orbit, and the whole planet from a million miles away.

panels.heading: ABI GeoColor on GOES-19
panels.blurb: A full disc of Earth every 10 minutes. ABI has no true green channel, so daytime GeoColor imagery synthesizes green from the red visible band, a near-infrared band, and blue, giving a true-color-like image at about 0.5-1 km per pixel. At night the same product switches to infrared cloud and fog data, with a fixed, pre-rendered city-lights layer (derived from separate satellite data, not live at the time of the shot) blended in over land.

panels.heading: EPIC on DSCOVR
panels.blurb: The full, sunlit disc of Earth, roughly a full hemisphere at a time. The camera actually captures ten separate monochrome exposures, one per filter; the "natural color" image combines three of them (approximately 443 nm blue, 551 nm green, and 680 nm red) into an RGB composite. Onboard averaging brings the native 2048x2048 frame down to about 1024x1024 pixels, roughly 25 km per pixel. New images arrive about every two hours.

subject: Sun
title: The Sun, 2026-09-16
intro: 6 views of the Sun from GOES, SDO, SOHO, ordered from the surface outward: the visible surface, then the hot corona in ultraviolet from two different spacecraft, then the outer corona seen by a coronagraph that blocks the disc.

candidate.title: SDO HMI intensitygram
candidate.credit: NASA/SDO and the AIA, EVE, and HMI science teams

panels.heading: HMI continuum on SDO
panels.blurb: HMI images the full disc at 4096x4096 pixels, roughly 1 arcsecond resolution, updating every 45 seconds. The continuum frame shows the granulated surface and any sunspots but carries none of the magnetic or velocity information HMI is actually built to measure.

candidate.title: SDO AIA 304 Å
candidate.credit: NASA/SDO and the AIA, EVE, and HMI science teams

panels.heading: AIA, 304 Å on SDO
panels.blurb: Each channel isolates one temperature layer of the solar atmosphere; the colours are false and assigned by convention. 304 Å, He II, about 50,000 K, red: chromosphere and prominences. 171 Å, Fe IX, about 630,000 K, gold: quiet corona and coronal loops. 193 Å, Fe XII (and Fe XXIV in flares), about 1.2 million K: corona and coronal holes. 211 Å, Fe XIV, about 2 million K: active regions. 335 Å, Fe XVI, about 2.5 million K: active regions. 94 Å, Fe XVIII, about 6 million K: flaring plasma. 131 Å, Fe VIII plus Fe XXI/XXIII, roughly 400,000 K to 16 million K: flares across a wide temperature range. 1600 Å, C IV plus continuum, about 100,000 K and 5,000 K: transition region and photosphere. 1700 Å, continuum, about 5,000 K: photosphere. Native frames are 4096x4096 pixels at 0.6 arcsec/pixel; this site uses NASA's 1024 px browse copies.

candidate.credit: NASA/SDO and the AIA, EVE, and HMI science teams

panels.heading: AIA, 193 Å on SDO

candidate.title: GOES SUVI 195 Å
candidate.credit: Helioviewer.org; data courtesy of the respective instrument teams

panels.heading: SUVI, 195 Å on GOES-19
panels.blurb: SUVI's six channels, 94, 131, 171, 195, 284 and 304 Å, sample much the same ions and temperatures as SDO/AIA and SOHO/EIT: about 630,000 K in 171 Å, several million K in 94 and 131 Å, and the cooler chromosphere in 304 Å. Its design and role closely mirror EIT's.

candidate.title: SDO AIA 211/193/171 composite
candidate.credit: NASA/SDO and the AIA, EVE, and HMI science teams

panels.heading: AIA 211/193/171 composite on SDO
panels.blurb: By standard convention, 211 Å (Fe XIV, about 2 million K) is mapped to red, 193 Å (Fe XII, about 1.2 million K) to green, and 171 Å (Fe IX, about 630,000 K) to blue, then combined. Corona bright in all three channels looks golden-white; structures bright mainly in the cooler 171 Å channel look blue; hotter, more disturbed plasma trends toward orange and red.

candidate.title: SOHO LASCO C2 white-light
candidate.credit: Helioviewer.org; data courtesy of the respective instrument teams

panels.heading: LASCO, C2 on SOHO
panels.blurb: Both are white-light cameras recording sunlight scattered by free electrons in the corona (Thomson scattering), not any particular wavelength. C2's occulting disc blocks the inner 1.5 solar radii and images out to about 6 solar radii; C3's disc blocks out to about 3.7 solar radii and images out to about 30 solar radii, a much wider but coarser view.

subject: Mars
title: Mars, 2026-09-17
intro: 4 recent images of Mars from Curiosity, MRO, Perseverance. Capture times are in the captions; a sol is a Mars day.

panels.heading: Navcam, left on Perseverance rover
panels.blurb: It's a normal wide-angle perspective, not a fisheye.

panels.heading: WATSON on Perseverance rover
panels.blurb: A 1600x1200-pixel color sensor behind a fixed macro lens with no optical zoom; instead the arm moves the whole camera to change scale, focusing from about 2cm off the surface out to infinity. Close up it resolves roughly 14 micrometers per pixel, coarsening to around 100 micrometers per pixel farther back.

panels.heading: Navcam on Curiosity rover
panels.blurb: Monochrome images with a 45-degree field of view, paired with its left-eye partner (NAV_LEFT_B) for stereo depth; mounted just below the A-side pair on the mast, aimed the same direction.

meta.description: The objective of this observation is to examine layers. In a large area in and around Arabia there are outcrops of layered terrain. HiRISE can see minute details that allows us to catalog different types of layers and to discover under what conditions they are produced. In this particular image there is a cap rock on top of some poorly formed layers and some well formed layers. (NASA/JPL-Caltech/University of Arizona)

panels.heading: HiRISE on Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter
panels.blurb: From MRO's roughly 300km orbit, HiRISE resolves about 0.3 meters per pixel - individual boulders and rover tracks are visible. It scans a long strip as the spacecraft flies overhead; the full-width detector is black and white, but a narrower strip down the center is also imaged in three color bands (blue-green 400-600nm, red 550-850nm, near-infrared 800-1000nm). A full frame can run to about 20,000 x 126,000 pixels.
